title: KMS Operator safeguards and secrets E2E upgrade notes (v0.1 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note collects operational safeguards, terraform module considerations, and a stepwise upgrade plan for rolling the KMS operator (and upstream HSM-backed KEK integration) in private deployments (VPC / on-prem). The goal is to define a low-risk path for customers running the operator that manages envelope keys, secret provisioning, and audit telemetry while preserving the ability to recover and validate audit trails after the upgrade.

Scope and context:
- Targets: private-deployments with customer-managed KMS (cloud or HSM-backed) integrated via the KMS Operator CRDs used by our on-prem stack.
- Includes: terraform modules (state migration notes), operator upgrade sequence, preflight checks, audit log verification, rollback/forensics play, and a small e2e test harness to run before canary.
- Excludes: hosted-api upgrades, dedicated-managed hardware procurement.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Terraform 1.4.x or later in use; remote state lives in customer-managed storage (S3/GCS/Minio) and is encrypted at rest.
- Customers may have HSMs (PKCS#11 or vendor API) or cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault). Operator must be able to bind to either.
- Minimal downtime requirement: online rolling upgrade preferred; brief maintenance windows allowed for migration of KEK wrapping metadata.

High-level upgrade objectives:
1) Ensure all active envelope keys (KEKs) are known and accessible (no orphaned ciphertext).
2) Verify audit log continuity pre/post upgrade; ensure append-only property where possible.
3) Migrate terraform state safely if TF provider schema changes (state-backed resource renames).
4) Maintain ability to perform emergency manual unwrap using escrowed material.
5) Add operator-level runtime guards to prevent accidental key deletion or key-schedule changes without confirmation.

Pre-upgrade preflight checklist (automated where feasible):
- Inventory check: list all keys, their IDs, creation timestamps, TTL/rotation schedules. Save as RECOVERY_KEYS-<date>.json.
- Verify HSM connectivity: run vendor PKCS#11 list-keys and confirm slot/cert mapping.
- Verify cloud KMS IAM: operator service account bound to crypto keys/encryption keys + decrypt/list permissions.
- Remote state snapshot: make a point-in-time copy of terraform remote state and store encrypted with customer-supplied PGP key.
- Audit log export: export last 90 days of audit events relating to /kms/* and /secrets/* (store checksums).
- Smoke tests: sign/verify an ephemeral payload using the KEK-derived wrapping key.
- Operator version compatibility matrix: confirm target operator binary supports the installed CRD version (if CRD change required, plan CRD migrate).

Terraform module notes (practical items):
- New input variables expected:
  - kms_operator_disable_auto_rotate (bool) - default false; recommend setting true during upgrade window.
  - hsm_pkcs11_module_path (string) - optional, only for on-prem HSMs.
  - key_escrow_bucket (string) - location where transient escrowed wrapped keys are written (encrypted).
  - tf_state_kms_key_id (string) - optional; ensure TF remote state encryption uses a stable master key.
- Outputs to surface:
  - kms_operator_crd_version (string)
  - primary_kek_id (string)
  - last_rotation_checkpoint (string timestamp)
- Migration considerations:
  - Avoid renaming resource addresses where possible. If unavoidable, use terraform state mv with the snapshot made earlier.
  - If module splits (e.g., moving key management from module A to module B), plan a two-step apply: first create new resources in parallel (dual-write metadata), then cutover.
  - Remote state lock timeout should be increased during upgrade to avoid conflicting automation.

Operator runtime safeguards to add (recommended as immediate follow-ups):
- Two-step destructive operations: any change that deletes keys or permanently changes key policy must set an annotation approved-by with a ticket id; operator will refuse otherwise.
- Read-only maintenance mode: settable via ConfigMap to ensure operator only serves reads and does not rotate or create keys during window.
- Op-level rate-limiting: guard concurrent rewrap operations to reduce HSM pressure.
- Mutation audit fence: operator writes a signed mutation preimage to audit ledger before applying changes (allows off-line verification).

Upgrade step-by-step plan (canary -> staggered rollout):
1) Canary environment (non-prod private cluster): apply full upgrade targeting a single non-production customer-like environment. Run e2e.
2) Preflight on customer: run the Preflight checklist (automated script shipped as binaries in repo).
3) Set operator to read-only maintenance mode (ConfigMap toggle) and disable auto-rotate via terraform var.
4) Take tf remote-state snapshot and export audit logs.
5) Apply operator upgrade (rolling pods) with reduced concurrency (maxUnavailable=1).
6) Verify operator health, reconcile loop, and check that no keys were unexpectedly rotated.
7) Run end-to-end secret unwrap/wrap test against sample workloads and verify ciphertexts decrypt correctly and results match checksums.
8) Re-enable normal mode and monitor 48h for any regression in latency/errors.

E2E test harness (minimal):
- Components:
  - test-client: issues create-secret, read-secret, simulate rotate via CRD.
  - audit-collector: tail audit stream and validate mutation preimages.
  - tf-snapshot-verifier: validates state file diffs are only expected changes.
- Success criteria:
  - 100% of created secrets decrypt after upgrade using both operator API and direct HSM unwrap (where possible).
  - No dropped audit entries and mutation preimages match applied changes.

Audit log verification and forensic readiness:
- Use an append-only external store for critical mutation events (e.g., write mutation hash to customer-owned S3 bucket or append to a WORM ledger).
- Maintain signed checkpoints: operator signs every batch of mutation events with a rotation-specific signing key; customer stores the public key and verifies chain.
- For forensics, include both operator-level logs and HSM vendor audit exports. Correlate by timestamp and operation id.

Failure modes and rollback playbook:
- Failure: operator fails to start due to CRD mismatch
  - Rollback: scale new pods down, reapply previous CRD/old operator image, validate reads, notify.
- Failure: some ciphertexts become undecryptable (missing KEK)
  - Rollback: pause operator, run manual unwrap using escrowed KEKs (RECOVERY_KEYS file), import resulting plaintext secrets into secure transient secret store, rewrap with stable KEK, restore.
- Failure: audit gap detected
  - Rollback: stop writes to secret-store, flush operator mutation preimages to escrow bucket, reconstruct events from HSM vendor logs, correlate.

Operational play notes (watch items during and after rollout):
- HSM queue depth and latency metrics (PKCS#11 ops/s).
- Operator reconciliation loops per minute. Spike indicates potential flapping.
- Secret consumer error rate (401/403/5xx).
- TF plan drift: unexpected diffs post-apply.

Post-upgrade hardening and follow-ups (to be tracked as tickets):
- Implement operator annotation enforcement (ticket ENGOPS-7433).
- Add terraform provider acceptance test that exercises state migration paths (ENG-TEST-201).
- Build a canonical recovery-runbook (playbook) with explicit command examples for manual unwrap/wrap.
- Add continuous audit verification pipeline (daily) that validates append-only property and mutation signature chain.

Practical snippets / examples (notes for engineers):
- TF state mv example (run only after snapshot):
  terraform state mv module.old_kms.redwood_kms_key.module.new_kms.redwood_kms_key

- Example operator maintenance toggle (kubectl edit configmap kms-operator-config):
  maintenanceMode: true
  allowedOps: [read, verify]

- Escrow encryption recommendation:
  - When writing RECOVERY_KEYS-<date>.json to customer escrow bucket, encrypt that file using the customer-supplied PGP key and store checksum in Concourse/CI artifact store.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Decide on default retention for mutation preimages (30d vs 90d) given storage costs and forensics needs.
- Define a standard format for mutation preimages that works across cloud KMS and PKCS#11 exports.
- Confirm whether operator should auto-reissue signing key when rotated, or rely on HSM signing key lifecycle.
- Add a smoke test that validates operator will refuse destructive changes without approved-by annotation (unit + e2e).

Appendix: quick runbook commands (cheat-sheet)
- Export audit logs: kubectl logs -n redwood kms-operator --since=720h | grep "mutation" > audit-export-<date>.log
- Snapshot TF remote state (S3 example): aws s3 cp s3://customer-tf-state/terraform.tfstate ./tfstate-<date>.backup --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id $TF_STATE_KMS
- Quick manual unwrap (HSM-backed): (vendor cli) hsm unwrap --key-id $KEK_ID --ciphertext-file secret.ct --out plaintext.bin

Notes to self: communicate plan with Solutions Eng and customer CISO at least 72 hours prior to scheduled upgrade. Provide escalation contacts for HSM vendor support.

End of draft.
